patch_commits.change: bound PAX value reads by TAR entry size
guard integer overflow in header length accounting
avoid allocate-then-fill pattern across archive parsers

vulnerable_api.root_cause: The PAX record declares a value length far larger than its containing TAR entry. Commons Compress 1.8.1 allocates a byte array using the declared record length before the stream reveals the short entry; the patched parser validates the record against the entry length before allocating.

observations.stdout: RESULT=java.io.IOException:Paxheader value size 99999985 exceeds size of header record
observations.result: malformed PAX record rejected before large allocation

first_party_call_path.minecraft_versions: 1.14 through 1.17.1 where the 1.8.1 manifest entry occurs
first_party_call_path.path: Realms world download UI -> Realm API request returns WorldDownload.downloadLink -> HTTP download of .tar.gz -> GzipCompressorInputStream -> TarArchiveInputStream.getNextTarEntry -> extraction.
first_party_call_path.source_bound_class_and_callsite_analysis: See the prior report for exact JAR hashes, mappings, and class SHA-256 values. The exact version metadata establishes org.apache.commons:commons-compress:1.8.1 and Commons IO 2.5 for Minecraft 1.14.4.
first_party_call_path.input_provenance: The download link is returned by the Mojang Realms API, and archive bytes are fetched over HTTPS. This probe proves the parser behavior and that the vanilla path reaches the parser, but it does not establish that a Realm owner can make the server emit this malformed PAX/TAR metadata or bypass server-side validation.
first_party_call_path.attacker_reachability: Unresolved. The Realms archive is server-produced; no controlled Realm or server-side archive-construction experiment was available.

finding_dispositions.technical_justification: The affected TAR API is reached by an optional vanilla Realms world-download path, and an isolated 2.5 KB gzip TAR reproduced OutOfMemoryError in the exact manifest library. The fixed upstream artifact rejects the same bytes. Whether a remote Realm operator can cause the service to deliver these inconsistent PAX length fields remains unverified; therefore the finding is not cleared.
finding_dispositions.reviewer: Codex automated technical investigation; independent human review pending
follow_up_requirements: Obtain a safe test Realm or server-generated archive demonstrating whether an owner-controlled world can preserve attacker-chosen PAX record lengths.
Request Mojang to update the affected game-managed Commons Compress library to a compatible fixed version.
Keep all three source-group occurrences blocking until attacker input and upstream remediation are resolved.
